title: Onboard & Quant Research Notes (wk of 2026-06-15)
body:
Sprint snapshot + weekly research standup (informal)
Owners: Maya (lead), Marco (experiments), Liang (infra + CI), Anika (eval harness)
Date range: 2026-06-15 -> 2026-06-21
Context / goal: move the new 7B int8 onboarding from exploratory -> candidate for sandbox serving. Reduce regressions vs fp16 (perplexity + safety probes) and validate KV-cache correctness under continuous batching.

Meeting cadence and attendees
- Mon 9:30 - quick sync (Maya, Marco, Liang) — decisions captured below
- Wed 11:00 - cross-team demo with SRE + serving-runtime (Priya attended)
- Fri 16:00 - retro + next-week plan (notes appended)

What we ran this week (experiments)
1) Int8 post-training quantization (PTQ) on 7B candidate (open-model-v2)
   - recipe: dynamic range calibration (128 steps), per-channel weight quant for linear layers, bias-preserve trick from notebook #q-ptq-06
   - infra: single A100-40GB, batch=1/seq=512 for calibration; inference runs on dedicated dev pool with continuous batching enabled
   - results: perplexity on eval-clean drops from 12.3 (fp16) -> 12.9 (int8 PTQ), ROUGE/QA latents show 0.6% average F1 drop on small qa set
   - perf: token throughput +18% vs fp16; memory footprint -28%
   - open issue: repeated token probability spikes for 0.3% of eval sequences (investigating rounding noise in attention softmax)

2) Quant-aware fine-tune (QAT) quick pass (10k steps)
   - recipe: fake-quant during training, 8-bit activations clipped; learning rate 3e-5 on LM head only for speed
   - results: perplexity recovers to 12.4 after QAT; QA F1 within 0.2% of fp16 baseline
   - cost: ~2.2x compute vs PTQ calibration; candidate for production only if regressions persist after other mitigations

3) KV-cache alignment validation under continuous batching
   - test: 1k randomized prompt traces, mixed seq lengths (32->1024) with interleaved requests causing concurrent KV eviction events
   - bug found: off-by-one in cached position index when contiguous requests cross batch boundaries (PR #1289 linked)
   - mitigation: hotfix in serving-runtime that aligns per-request pos offsets; deployed to dev pool 6/19 for smoke testing
   - impact: previously observed 0.4% inconsistent next-token divergence reduced to ~0.01% (statistical noise)

4) Safety/evals: regression probes + hallucination checks
   - harness: Anika's eval runner v0.7 (docker image: rwinf/aml-eval:v0.7) using prompt suite: commonsense QA, instruction-following, and safety-red-team set
   - find: on instruction-following prompts with long context (>600 tokens) int8 PTQ more likely to drop long-range entity references (~1.1% more hallucinations). QAT reduces this to 0.2% over baseline

Decisions made this week
- Do not promote PTQ int8 directly to sandbox serving yet; require at least one QAT pass or aggressive hybrid strategy (int8 weights + fp16 attention softmax) to reduce long-range failures. (Assigned: Marco, due 2026-06-28)
- Merge KV-cache alignment hotfix (PR #1289) to staging and add regression suite that replays interleaved traces daily. (Assigned: Liang, done 2026-06-19 for staging)
- Add 'long-context hallucination' test to the nightly eval matrix with threshold alerts. (Assigned: Anika, ticket ML-3302)

Open questions / discussion items
- Where to draw the line for QAT cost vs benefit? If QAT ~2x compute but reduces hallucinations by >70% it might be acceptable for high-value customers. Need cost model per request (Maya + Finance).
- Hybrid numeric path: experiment idea — keep attention softmax in fp16 while quantizing matmuls to int8 (will require kernel support). Should prototype network fusion to avoid copy penalties.
- Calibration dataset sensitivity: our small calibration corpus (10k tokens) may bias distribution; need diversity sweep (legal docs, long-form chat, code)

Action items (owner / due / notes)
- Marco: run QAT full head-only sweep (3 lr seeds) and provide evaluation matrix by 2026-06-25 (priority: perplexity + long-context hallucination rate)
- Liang: add daily interleaved trace replay job to CI (use 2x dev pool) and surface divergence metrics to Console; due 2026-06-23
- Anika: add long-context hallucination test to nightly evals, implement alerting rule (threshold: >0.5% increase vs baseline) due 2026-06-24; link to ML-3302
- Maya: cost sensitivity write-up for QAT vs PTQ for leadership (short memo) due 2026-06-29
- SRE/Priya: monitor staging after PR #1289 for memory anomalies (esp under burst mode) — smoke test window 6/19-6/22

Quick experiment notes (raw)
- calibration-6b-128steps.log: observed heavy tail of 1e-4 activations in 3rd transformer block; suspect outlier tokens from tokenizer unknown handling
- qat-run-06-17: checkpoint saved at step 10k -> saved size ~9.1GB (fp16 baseline 12.8GB)
- eval-longctx-1000.json: sample-level diffs attached in linked artifacts (Confluence page)

Risks / mitigation
- Risk: releasing int8 with KV misalignment will lead to subtle correctness regressions in customers with conversational workloads. Mitigation: lock version until KV fix + nightly regression pass
- Risk: QAT increases infra cost. Mitigation: only apply QAT to final candidate models we plan to offer on Dedicated; leave PTQ for trial customers with clear warnings

Notes to self / half-baked ideas
- Try per-sequence dynamic rescaling of activations during inference for long-context traces rather than retraining (cheap heuristic)
- Investigate third-party kernels for mixed-int hybrid softmax (email vendor team)
- Add a short 'readme-for-onboarding' section for PMs summarizing tradeoffs in plain English (one-pager)

Friday retro highlights (2026-06-18 meeting)
- Wins: KV bug triaged and hotfixed faster than expected; QAT shows promising recovery on long-context tasks
- Frustrations: eval harness flaky on a subset of long token traces (investigate corrupt samples)
- Next week focus: finish QAT sweep, harden nightly evals, prepare a candidate summary for product review

Appendix (links & quick refs)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1289 (KV-cache fix)
- Jira: ML-3245 (7B int8 onboarding epic), ML-3302 (long-context hallucination test)
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/AM/quant-onboarding-guide (calibration recipes + eval summaries)

End of note.
(Informal capture — will convert to a short slide & a 1-page memo if leadership wants a summary.)
